clue.text: Entertainment at which a dog involuntarily stole the show!

definitions.text: Entertainment at which a dog involuntarily stole the show!

parts.words: Entertainment at which a dog involuntarily stole the show!
parts.note: a show whose tiny performers live on animals: a dog wandering by would carry the whole cast away in its coat without meaning to

explanation.surface: A mutt wanders on stage and accidentally upstages every performer.
explanation.definitionFit: A travelling sideshow where trained insects supposedly pull carts and perform tricks.

clue.text: Home that's not sparkling

definitions.meaning: an apartment, a dwelling on one floor
a drink that has lost its fizz

explanation.definitionFit: An apartment is a place to live; a drink gone still has no bubbles.

clue.text: An inveterate follower, from that day on

definitions.meaning: someone forever coming behind: always (ever) behind (after)
the fairy-tale phrase for permanently, from then onwards

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is cryptic: split the phrase into two words, one meaning always and the other meaning behind, and you have an inveterate follower.
explanation.definitionFit: The fairy-tale close says the couple lived happily from that moment forward, permanently.

clue.text: Stop after me, in this instance

definitions.text: Stop after me, in this instance

parts.words: Stop after me, in this instance
parts.note: a stop is a punctuation mark, and in this very clue the mark printed straight after the word me is the one wanted

explanation.surface: Someone tells a follower to halt behind them on this occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: Look at the clue as printed: the punctuation mark sitting after 'me' is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A punctuation mark indicating a short pause in a sentence, like the one after 'me' here.

clue.text: Come by and you welcome hospitably

definitions.meaning: to obtain or get hold of something
to greet and entertain guests

explanation.definitionFit: To get something sent to you, and to greet guests formally, as a host does.

clue.text: Overlooked, not being well-known

parts.note: UN is a prefix meaning not
noted means famous or well known

explanation.surface: Someone was passed over because they were not famous.
explanation.definitionFit: Something overlooked went unobserved, never remarked upon.

clue.text: Mad to make a comeback, but have a try

indicators.note: coming back means the word for mad is read from right to left

parts.note: bats is slang for crazy

explanation.surface: A crazy person returns but makes an attempt anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make a comeback' turns BATS round.
explanation.definitionFit: To take a stab at something is to attempt it.

clue.text: Wake and have a work-out?

definitions.meaning: the trail left behind something moving, like the trailing part of a gown or a ship's track
to exercise, as an athlete does in preparation

explanation.walkthrough: 'Wake' looks like a verb about waking up; it is the trail that follows behind a moving thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A trail following behind, like a bridal gown's; and to exercise regularly for fitness.

clue.text: Resentment of the ladybird?

definitions.meaning: a sour, aggrieved feeling
the lady bird here is a female marsh heron, named with the feminine ending as in lioness

explanation.walkthrough: A ladybird is not the beetle but a female bird: the bittern is a heron, and adding the feminine -ESS ending gives its female.
explanation.definitionFit: Resentment is sour feeling, an acrid grudge held against someone.

clue.text: Cheat over the land bond

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece over another is placed above it, so it comes first

parts.note: to con is to cheat or swindle
a tract is an area of land

explanation.surface: Someone swindles their way into a deal over property.
explanation.definitionFit: A legally binding agreement between parties.

clue.text: Alight to one side of the ship

definitions.meaning: read as two words, a light, which is a beam

definitions.text: to one side of the ship
definitions.meaning: nautical term for at right angles to the keel, off the vessel's side

explanation.walkthrough: 'Alight' looks like 'on fire' or 'get off'; split it as 'a light' and a light is a beam.
explanation.definitionFit: Nautical: lying at right angles to the vessel's length, directly off its side.

clue.text: Can't carry on, son. Not!

annotationWithheld.why: Can't carry on, son. Not! — wordplay C(ON SON)ANT (CANT carrying ON + SON) is clear, but 'Not!' does not define CONSONANT as held; likely garbled in OCR.

clue.text: He thinks men will never be able to change a lot

definitions.text: He thinks men will never be able to change a lot

parts.words: He thinks men will never be able to change a lot
parts.note: one's lot is one's destiny; this believer holds that people cannot alter what fate deals them, while the surface suggests a cynic about male behaviour

explanation.surface: A cynic believes men will hardly ever change much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot' looks like 'much'; it is one's lot in life, destiny.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone believing that all events are predetermined and human effort cannot alter destiny.

clue.text: Anxious at first in the extreme

indicators.note: the word IN stands at the start, so taking it off the front of the extreme word leaves the answer

parts.note: intense means existing in an extreme degree

explanation.surface: Someone who was extremely nervous right at the beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: Put IN at the front of the answer and you get INTENSE, 'in the extreme'; so the answer is that word with its leading IN dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Being anxious means being nervous and strained, wound up.

clue.text: An unattached female?

parts.note: read as a woman come untied or let loose rather than single, the phrase for a promiscuous woman

explanation.surface: A single woman, not in any relationship.
explanation.definitionFit: A dated term for a woman considered promiscuous or of easy morals.

clue.text: Consequence of obtaining one's release?

definitions.meaning: a result of something
read as two words, being freed is to come out

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reverses the phrase 'come out', as a released prisoner does.
explanation.definitionFit: A result or end product of an action or process.

clue.text: To get an aerial picture, went too far

definitions.meaning: read as two words, a photograph taken from above
passed beyond the target

explanation.definitionFit: A photo taken from above, and the past tense of going past a target.

clue.text: Revealing nothing, is it buried in a kitchen cupboard?

definitions.meaning: expressionless, showing no emotion

definitions.text: is it buried in a kitchen cupboard?
definitions.meaning: a cooking vessel laid to rest, as if interred in the cupboard

explanation.walkthrough: The second half reads the answer as two words: a deceased piece of cookware.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing no expression, as a comedian telling a joke with a straight face.

clue.text: He has no chaps, Dad, to cover the strange events

indicators.note: the father's letters go round the others, covering them on each side

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
taken as written
taken as written
men, as chaps are blokes

explanation.surface: A man with no sons asks his father to deal with odd happenings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cover' signals a container: the father's word wraps round the rest; 'has' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Remarkable occurrences, as in phenomena unexplained by science.

clue.text: Artist who never got a commission, we hear

indicators.note: the word is pronounced like the painter's name

parts.note: a non-commissioned officer, an army rank below the officers

explanation.surface: A painter who was never hired for a portrait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'commission' suggests a paid painting job; it is an officer's rank. John Singer Sargent was a famous American-born portrait painter.
explanation.definitionFit: John Singer Sargent, American portrait painter of the late nineteenth century.

clue.text: Hard work, being upright, will get you somewhere

annotationWithheld.why: Hard work, being upright, will get you somewhere — 'Hard work' defines TRAVAIL, but no parse of 'being upright, will get you somewhere' gives its letters as held; possibly a garbled or misread clue.
annotationWithheld.clue: Hard work, being upright, will get you somewhere

clue.text: The better they are, the more they get one down

definitions.text: The better they are, the more they get one down

parts.words: The better they are, the more they get one down
parts.note: golf clubs used on the green: a good one sinks the ball into the hole, while the surface suggests depressing people

explanation.surface: The more skilled some people are, the more they depress you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get one down' sounds like 'make you sad'; in golf it means sinking the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Golf clubs with flat faces used to roll the ball on the green toward the hole.

clue.text: Fixes the little rascals!

definitions.meaning: tight spots, predicaments
mischievous children, as a parent might fondly call them

explanation.definitionFit: Awkward predicaments, and the affectionate term for naughty children.

clue.text: Hearing knocks, covers up

indicators.note: listening to the word for knocks gives the same sound as the answer

parts.note: raps are knocks on a door

explanation.surface: Someone hears banging and pulls the blankets over themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrap is to enclose or swathe.

clue.text: Man induced inflammation

parts.note: inflammation read as setting things on fire, deliberately caused by a person, rather than a medical swelling

explanation.surface: A doctor notes swelling brought on by a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inflammation' sounds medical; here it is a fire, started deliberately.
explanation.definitionFit: The criminal act of deliberately setting fire to property.

clue.text: A provider of stock ingredients

parts.note: stock read as family line rather than soup base: a forebear contributes the elements of one's lineage

explanation.surface: A supplier of soup-making items like bones and vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stock' suggests broth; it is lineage, the descent of a family.
explanation.definitionFit: A forebear, someone from whom a person descends.

clue.text: Stretches the wrong way and breaks

indicators.note: taken in the opposite direction, so the word for stretches runs backwards

parts.note: spans are stretches, as of time or distance

explanation.surface: A rubber band pulled the wrong way breaks.
explanation.definitionFit: Breaks suddenly, as a twig cracks in two.

clue.text: Action brought by a patient

definitions.meaning: a lawsuit taken to court
doctors speak of a patient under their care in this way

explanation.definitionFit: A legal suit taken to court, and the medical word for a person being treated.

clue.text: In particular, doctors have to take a drop

parts.note: MOs are medical officers, army doctors
taken as written
a fall is a drop

explanation.surface: Doctors in particular must take a tumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Above everything else, especially.

clue.text: At an age for retirement from the ring

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so both pieces together are read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
an era is an age

explanation.surface: A boxer leaves the ring at the age to retire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for retirement' turns both pieces round together; 'At' and 'from' are link words, and the ring is a boxing ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxing ring is an enclosed area for contests.

clue.text: Figure it makes one cross

parts.note: in Roman numerals, one (I) followed by a cross (X) makes this number

explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like angry; it is the X shape. IX is this number in Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: The number written IX in Roman numerals, between eight and ten.

clue.text: As she stirred in the spice, near disaster!

indicators.note: the stirred letters go into the spice word

parts.note: clove is a spice

indicators.note: stirring mixes these letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A cook stirs spice into a dish and nearly ruins it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stirred' is the anagram signal on the two little words, and 'in' places the result inside the spice, splitting it after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow escape from danger or calamity.
